newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tightens security after prison revolts.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tightens security after prison revolts.

text.p: Bangladesh on Friday beefed up security at the nation's prisons to prevent further unrest as rebellious prisoners holding two jails refused to surrender.
Extra police and paramilitary troops were posted inside and around prisons across the country, police said.

A revolt at Jessore Jail in western Bangladesh entered its fifth day on Friday. The uprising began on Monday when prisoners armed with knives and iron bars frightened away guards and took control of the complex.
About 2,000 police and troops have surrounded the jail.
On Thursday, prisoners in northwestern Tangail Jail also rebelled, taking five jail officials hostage.
A third revolt in southern Barisal Jail was foiled quickly on Thursday by prison guards who subdued rioting prisoners armed with iron rods and bricks after a fight lasting about an hour.
The trouble started after 90 prisoners were freed under a nationwide amnesty marking the country's 25th independence anniversary on Monday.
Angered at being left out of the amnesty, prisoners at the three jails have rioted, with some demanding freedom and others seeking better treatment and food, police said.
"All efforts to peacefully end the jail crises have apparently failed after the prisoners refused to give up. We have not yet decided whether to use force to end the crisis," said one police officer.
